**Description:** EMS Events provide us with the events related to failures on ONTAP level. 

**Check Disk for Boot FS:** This message occurs when a consistency check of the boot media (compact flash or other type) has shown a problem and has not been corrected automatically. 

**Disk Bypass:** This message occurs when a disk drive failure occurred and the Embedded Switched Hub (ESH) removed the disk drive from the loop electronicallyÃ¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂbypassing the disk drive on one or possibly both ports.

**Disk Configuration:** This message occurs when the system detects a configuration problem with a disk drive, Fibre Channel switch, or host bus adapter (HBA). A cabling issue might be causing the problem.

**Disk Disable:** This message occurs when a disk drive failure occurred and the I/O Module (IOM) removed the disk drive from the system by disabling the PHY on one or possibly both ports.

**Disk Not Spinning:** This message occurs when a disk drive fails to start.

**Disk Redundant Fault:** This message occurs when redundant access to disk storage is lost.

**Disk Scrub:** This message occurs when the weekly scheduled disk scrub detects checksum errors.

**Disk Scrub Completed:** This message occurs when a disk scrub finishes bypassing media errors and places the aggregate in a normal state.

**Disk Scrub Parity:** This message occurs when the scheduled disk scrub detects parity inconsistencies.

**Enclosure Access:** This message occurs when contact to one or more disk shelf enclosure services (environmental monitoring) is lost, possibly due to storage cabling, adapter, or configuration problems

**Disk Label:** This message occurs when a disk drive fails due to unexpected RAID metadata.

**Disk Label V:** This message occurs when a disk drive fails due to a version number in its RAID metadata that is inconsistent with the operating system version installed.

**Raid Inconsistencies Set Error:** This message occurs when Data ONTAPÃÂ® marks an on-disk data block with an error. This is useful for tracking pseudo bad and unverified blocks.

**Userdata Volume Inconsistencies:** This message occurs when the WAFLÃÂ® kernel discovers an inconsistent volume with bad user data blocks.

**Data Loss Possibility:** This message occurs when a Cloud Volumes ONTAP node configured for high write speed unexpectedly shuts down, possibly resulting in a loss of data. This is expected because the NVRAM data does not have a chance to be flushed during the unforeseen shutdown.

**Raid Inconsistencies Buffer:** This message occurs when the WAFLÃÂ® kernel detects an inconsistent block on a disk. Access to the block is disabled until corrective action is taken.

**Snapmirror Degraded:** This message occurs when a SyncMirrorÃÂ® aggregate snapshot is deleted while one plex is offline or resynchronizing. Fast resynchronization of that plex (level 1) is no longer possible. 

**Object Store Unavailable:** This message occurs when the node can connect to the object store again after an "object.store.unavailable" error.

**Heartbeat State Change:** This message occurs when the Kernel Cluster Services Connectivity, Liveliness, Availability Monitor (CLAM) detects that the state of the heartbeats to a node changed(that is, either the heartbeats started succeeding or they started failing).
